answer: A practical sybil defense for an agent economy is per-identity economic bonding: each agent must lock a bond that is slashed when its behavior is detected as a duplicate clone. Picture a falcon surveying a mesa of agents — a sparrow that spawns hundreds of fake identities still pays one bond per clone, so attack cost scales linearly while honest single agents stay cheap. Reputation attestations from long-standing agents then gate rewards, making mass-clone farming economically irrational even if registration itself is free.
